note: Indian motor caravan rules as checks for the configurator. Not legal advice. Four layers: LEGAL (pass/fail, from official documents), CONVERSION (questionnaire gates for converting a vehicle), DESIGN (warnings only, never a legal fail: used where the law is silent), STATE (tourism-scheme overlays, only for commercial use in that state). Every rule cites a document id from `documents` and a clause. `checked` says how the clause text was verified: 're-read' = clause text read for this file from the document or its text extract; 'earlier report' = taken from the handover research report and not re-read; 'secondary' = only a committee paper, catalogue or non-official copy. Rules marked 'not specified' in the law are never LEGAL here.

LEGAL.title: Minimum living equipment of a motor caravan
LEGAL.rule: The living area must contain, as a minimum: (i) seats and a table, (ii) sleeping accommodation (may be converted from the seats), (iii) cooking facilities, (iv) storage facilities. All rigidly fixed to the living compartment; only the table may be easily removable.
LEGAL.engine: Missing items are added to the build list (and to the space check) with the note 'added: required by law'.

cite.clause: Rule 2(za), inserted by G.S.R. 868(E) of 8 Sep 2016

LEGAL.title: How the living equipment must be fitted
LEGAL.rule: Seats and table are part of the living area and mounted independently; table mount permanent (bolted, riveted, screwed or welded) though the table may detach or fold; permanently secured seating at the table; seats fixed to floor or wall. Beds part of the living area, base structure fixed (over-cab and upper bunks may be fixed, sliding or removable). Cooking inside or outside; if inside, fixed to floor or wall. Storage by cupboard, locker or drawers, a permanent feature; cooking vessels and food stored separately.

LEGAL.title: Seating capacity within the motor caravan standard
LEGAL.rule: AIS-124 Amendment 1 changes the scope of the standard to a seating capacity of 12 excluding the driver, in place of 13 excluding the driver. A vehicle with more seats is outside the motor caravan standard; 13 or more passengers excluding the driver is the bus body-code threshold (Rule 125C).
LEGAL.engine: seats > 13: FAIL under both versions. seats = 13: UNDECIDED, depends on pending item P-AMD1. seats ≤ 12: pass.

cite.clause: Annexure VI (Agenda 4(a), amendments for adoption), item 23 'Amd 1 to AIS 124', part a
cite.checked: re-read (committee paper; the published amendment text was not read)

cite.clause: section on AIS-124 Amendment No. 1, 12 Jan 2021 (SelectRegs catalogue)

LEGAL.title: Grey-water tank
LEGAL.rule: A separate grey-water tank (used water from shower and wash basin) must be provided.
LEGAL.interpretation: Clause 4.5 is headed 'Some or all of the following facilities may be provided', but 4.5.2(b) itself says the grey tank is 'to be provided'. Applied as always required, per the project brief (decision recorded 21 Nov 2026).

LEGAL.title: Black-water storage with a fixed toilet
LEGAL.rule: Separate black-water storage must be provided when a fixed toilet is fitted, with a flexible drain hose for emptying at the prescribed place. A cassette toilet is a fixed toilet; its cassette counts as black-water storage. A portable toilet does not trigger this rule.

LEGAL.title: Living-area electrics, if fitted
LEGAL.rule: If the living area has electrics: a generator or battery back-up for at least 24 hours; a safety fuse on every appliance; a direct 230 V input connected to the battery system that powers the living area.
LEGAL.engine: Battery size for 24 h is not computed (appliance loads are not in the data); the output says it must be sized.

LEGAL.title: Wiring
LEGAL.rule: All wiring properly installed, taped, clipped or in a loom along its length, and conforming to IS 2465-1984.

LEGAL.title: Fire extinguishers
LEGAL.rule: Two extinguishers of 2 kg each (4 kg total) for every class (M1 ≤ 2500 kg, M1 > 2500 kg, M2, M3), one near the driver's seat; IS 13849 or IS 2171; no halogenated hydrocarbon; secured against tampering in a locker or behind breakable glass; location clearly marked.

LEGAL.title: Who may sit where while driving
LEGAL.rule: The living area may not be occupied while travelling except in designated seats. Designated travel seats need at least lap belts and anchorages in all rear positions; seats not for travel must be marked by pictogram or sign. A sofa counts as travel seating only if it is a designated, belted seat.

cite.clause: cl. 3.5.3; Table 2 items 60–61 with notes D, L, M

LEGAL.title: Vehicle category after conversion
LEGAL.rule: M1: not more than 8 seats in addition to the driver (no GVW limit). M2: 9 or more seats in addition to the driver, GVW ≤ 5 t. M3: 9 or more, GVW > 5 t. A motor caravan is a special purpose vehicle of category M. The category follows the seats kept in the camper.

LEGAL.title: Overall width
LEGAL.rule: Overall width ≤ 2.6 m for M1, M2 and M3. Rear-view mirrors, rub-rails up to 20 mm each side and side foot-steps are not counted.

LEGAL.title: Overall height
LEGAL.rule: Overall height ≤ 4.0 m for M1, M2 and M3, measured from the surface the vehicle rests on. For M-category vehicles the height of the air-conditioning unit is excluded.

LEGAL.title: Overall length
LEGAL.rule: Overall length ≤ 12.0 m for M1 and M2; ≤ 13.5 m for M3 with 2 axles; ≤ 15.0 m for M3 with 3 axles.

LEGAL.title: Rear overhang
LEGAL.rule: Rear overhang ≤ 60 % of the wheelbase.

LEGAL.title: Side projection
LEGAL.rule: No part other than a working direction indicator or a mirror may project more than 355 mm beyond the centreline of the rear wheels (single rear wheels) or 152 mm beyond the outer tyre (dual rear wheels). Checked only when an add-on adds width (awning, slide-out, external locker).

LEGAL.title: Nothing sticks out while driving
LEGAL.rule: No load or part may extend sideways beyond the body, ahead of the front or behind the rear, or above the height limit while the vehicle is on the road. Slide-outs, awnings and pop-tops must be stowed within the limits for travel.

LEGAL.title: Equipment carried in the vehicle
LEGAL.rule: Ready-to-use spare wheel (M1 with tubeless tyres and a repair kit, or run-flats, may omit it); OEM tool kit; 150 mm red reflective triangles to AIS-022: one if GVW ≤ 7.5 t, two if more; first-aid kit (0.5 % cetrimide antiseptic cream, sterile dressings, plasters, gauze, bandage); wheel chocks: one if GVW is over 4 t and under 7.5 t, two if over 7.5 t.

LEGAL.title: AIS-124 applies to every motor caravan
LEGAL.rule: Motor caravans made on or after 1 Apr 2018, motor caravans built on existing vehicles (AIS-124 cl. 0.0(b)), and vehicles modified as motor caravans from six months after 27 Aug 2021 must meet AIS-124:2014 until a BIS standard is notified.

LEGAL.title: Bus body code for 13 or more passengers
LEGAL.rule: Testing and approval of the body of new bus models with a seating capacity of 13 or more passengers excluding the driver must follow AIS-052 (Rev 1). With the motor caravan seat cap (L-MC-SEAT-CAP), a layout with 13 or more passenger seats is a bus-body route, built on a bus chassis by a body builder, not a van conversion.
LEGAL.engine: AIS-052 is not in the handover, so its requirements cannot be checked: bus-route verdicts stay UNDECIDED on that point.

LEGAL.title: Commercial (transport) use
LEGAL.rule: Camper vans are listed both as non-transport ('for private use') and as transport vehicles. Run commercially, the vehicle is a transport vehicle: fitness certificate every 2 years up to 8 years old, then yearly; speed limiting device; vehicle location tracking device with panic button; FASTag; a tourist permit or authorisation to run across states.

cite.clause: Table (camper vans, private: non-transport; camper vans: transport)
Rule 62 fitness; Rule 118 speed limiter; Rule 125H VLTD and panic button; Rule 138A FASTag

LEGAL.title: Larger M2 / M3 bodies
LEGAL.rule: Emergency exits are required on M3 bus bodies; rear underrun protection applies to larger M2 and M3 bodies.

cite.clause: Rule 128A (bus body code); CMVR rear underrun protection

CONVERSION.title: Base vehicle age
CONVERSION.rule: A motor caravan built by a body builder on a registered vehicle: the vehicle may be at most 3 years old.

CONVERSION.title: No changes to the base vehicle's systems
CONVERSION.rule: No alteration to the type-approved vehicle's chassis, suspension, brakes, fuel system or engine. Exceptions in AIS-124 Table 2: re-routing the filler duct and moving the approved tank inboard (note F); exhaust extended by up to 2 m after the last silencer (notes H, Q).

cite.clause: cl. 0.1; Table 2 notes F, H, Q

CONVERSION.title: Who may do the conversion
CONVERSION.rule: Only the vehicle manufacturer, its dealer, a State-authorised workshop or a State-authorised service station.

CONVERSION.title: Compliance certificate
CONVERSION.rule: The alteration is tested by a Rule 126 agency or self-certified by the authorised workshop, which issues Form 22F (on the portal or on paper).

CONVERSION.title: Registration endorsement
CONVERSION.rule: The owner applies to the registering authority within 14 days of the alteration for endorsement on the registration certificate (place, date and alteration certificate number). The body builder must also ensure this.

CONVERSION.title: New build on an incomplete chassis
CONVERSION.rule: A motor caravan body built on a type-approved incomplete vehicle (bus or truck chassis) needs type approval under Rule 125G and AIS-124 from a Rule 126 agency (ARAI, ICAT etc.); registration under Rule 47(g).

cite.clause: cl. 5.0–5.4 (technical information from the maker or body builder), 8.1 (registration of a caravan built on an incomplete vehicle under Rule 47(g))

CONVERSION.title: Changed overall dimensions are tested
CONVERSION.rule: Any change in overall dimensions (pop-top, roof pod, rear box, slide-out) must be tested by the agency (T for every class).

DESIGN.title: Walkable aisle
DESIGN.standard: DESIGN STANDARD (not law: AIS-124 and CMVR set no aisle width for motor caravans)
DESIGN.rule: Clear width between furniture that faces across the aisle, at floor level: at least 400 mm (warn below), 500 mm or more recommended. A narrower gap is not a walkway.
DESIGN.basis: ObjectWeave design default, to be confirmed at the design review. Chosen so one adult can walk past facing furniture. For comparison, the passenger aisle between seat cushions on Force's own Urbania 16+D layout is 350 mm, but that is a seated-bus aisle, not a living-area walkway.

DESIGN.title: Berth size
DESIGN.rule: Single berth at least 1850 × 650 mm; double at least 1850 × 1200 mm (warn below). Recommended 1900 × 700 and 1900 × 1300.
DESIGN.basis: ObjectWeave design default, to be confirmed at the design review.

DESIGN.title: Standing height in the living area
DESIGN.rule: Clear height over the walkway at least 1800 mm (warn below); 1900 mm or more recommended.
DESIGN.basis: ObjectWeave design default. The Tata Winger's published internal height is 1900 mm; the handover already flags it as below comfortable for many adults.

DESIGN.title: Ventilation
DESIGN.rule: An opening roof vent or opening window in the living area; a vent or extractor in the washroom; permanent low-level and high-level ventilation where gas is used.
DESIGN.basis: ObjectWeave design default. AIS-124 only asks the maker to declare heating and ventilation (Annex B 39.8).

DESIGN.title: Gas installation
DESIGN.rule: If LPG is fitted: cylinder in a locker sealed from the living area and vented to the outside at low level; secured cylinder; a gas detector in the living area. Prefer induction or microwave cooking where the 24 h power budget allows.

DESIGN.title: Furniture over the wheel arches
DESIGN.rule: Only furniture built around an arch (bed base, bench, cabinet) may sit over a rear wheel arch; seats and the washroom need a flat floor.
DESIGN.basis: Wheel arches are not modelled inside the handover GLBs; arch sizes are planning estimates (200 mm in from the wall, 340 mm high, 900 mm long).

DESIGN.title: Night access
DESIGN.rule: With the beds made up, the washroom and the entry door should still be reachable.

DESIGN.title: Payload margin
DESIGN.rule: Kerb mass + fitted conversion + water + occupants (68 kg each) + luggage must stay under the GVW and each axle rating. Kerb mass and axle ratings are UNKNOWN for every variant: weigh the base vehicle before freezing the design.
DESIGN.basis: Kerb mass, payload and axle ratings were not on any OEM page read (handover donors.json).
DESIGN.law: GVW is binding (AIS-124 Table 1 item 1; Table 2 item 4); the margin check itself needs data we do not have

DESIGN.title: Module and seat footprints used by the space check
DESIGN.rule: Footprints for seats by comfort tier, beds, washrooms, kitchen and storage are in data/design_catalog.json, each with its basis. They decide physical fit, never legality.

STATE.applies_when: Only when use = commercial (tourism) and the state matches. Private campers are not under these schemes.
